title: Gorgeous George on Early Television
description: Gorgeous George's flamboyant act made him one of television's first stars and showed how a wrestling character could reach far beyond the ring.
source_material: Television wrestling broadcasts from 11 November 1947 (first TV appearance); Gorgeous George (Wikipedia); WWE.com Hall of Fame profile; Slam Wrestling profile
context_statement: Gorgeous George turned the wrestling gimmick into mass entertainment on early television, and figures as different as Muhammad Ali, James Brown and Bob Dylan later named him as an influence.
external_links: Gorgeous George (Wikipedia) (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gorgeous_George); Slam Wrestling: Gorgeous George (https://slamwrestling.net/legend/gorgeous-george/)

title: Rikidōzan & Masahiko Kimura vs. the Sharpe Brothers, 1954
event_name: JWA tour opening, Kuramae Kokugikan, Tokyo
wrestlers_involved: Rikidōzan; Masahiko Kimura; Ben Sharpe; Mike Sharpe
description: Tag matches broadcast on Japan's new television networks that made Rikidōzan a national hero and started professional wrestling's boom in Japan.
source_material: JWA cards from 19 February 1954, broadcast on NHK and NTV; Puroresu.com 1950s chronology; Rikidōzan (Wikipedia); Robert Whiting, "Remembering Rikidozan, the Sharpe Brothers, Masahiko Kimura and the Destroyer"
context_statement: Watched by crowds gathered around public television sets, these matches made Rikidōzan a national hero and founded professional wrestling as a major part of Japanese popular culture.
external_links: Puroresu.com: the 1950s (https://www.puroresu.com/history/1950s); Robert Whiting: Remembering Rikidozan and the Sharpe Brothers (https://robertwhiting.substack.com/p/remembering-rikidozan-the-sharpe)

title: Big Daddy vs. Giant Haystacks, Wembley Arena 1981
event_name: Wembley Arena, shown on ITV World of Sport
wrestlers_involved: Big Daddy (Shirley Crabtree); Giant Haystacks (Martin Ruane)
description: The long-awaited meeting of British wrestling's biggest hero and biggest villain, at Wembley Arena and on Saturday afternoon television.
source_material: Wembley Arena card, 18 June 1981, shown on ITV World of Sport later that month; itvwrestling.co.uk ratings history; Big Daddy and Giant Haystacks (Wikipedia); Pro Wrestling Stories
context_statement: Big Daddy against Giant Haystacks was British wrestling's defining feud of the television era, and its Wembley match marked the peak of wrestling's place in British Saturday-afternoon culture.
external_links: Pro Wrestling Stories: Big Daddy vs. Giant Haystacks (https://prowrestlingstories.com/pro-wrestling-stories/big-daddy-giant-haystacks-british-wrestling/); ITV wrestling: television ratings (https://itvwrestling.co.uk/ratings.html)

title: Kinnikuman
description: A Japanese manga and anime about superhuman wrestlers whose tournaments, tag teams and signature holds brought wrestling storytelling to a generation of readers and viewers.
source_material: Kinnikuman manga by Yudetamago (Weekly Shōnen Jump, 1979–1987); Toei Animation anime series (Nippon Television, from 3 April 1983); Kinnikuman (Wikipedia); Mental Floss on M.U.S.C.L.E. figures
context_statement: Kinnikuman built a hugely popular manga and anime on the tropes of professional wrestling, and through its toys reached children in North America who had never read the original.
external_links: Kinnikuman (Wikipedia) (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kinnikuman); Mental Floss: a brief history of M.U.S.C.L.E. figures (https://www.mentalfloss.com/article/31625/brief-history-muscle-figures)

title: Flair vs. Steamboat: The 1989 Trilogy
event_name: Chi-Town Rumble, Clash of the Champions VI and WrestleWar '89
wrestlers_involved: Ric Flair; Ricky Steamboat; Lou Thesz; Pat O'Connor; Terry Funk
description: Three NWA World Heavyweight Championship matches between February and May 1989, nominated together as a composite work of in-ring storytelling.
source_material: NWA Chi-Town Rumble pay-per-view (UIC Pavilion, Chicago, 20 February 1989); Clash of the Champions VI broadcast on TBS (Louisiana Superdome, New Orleans, 2 April 1989); WrestleWar '89 pay-per-view (Nashville, 7 May 1989); WWE.com interview with Flair and Steamboat
context_statement: Across three matches in eleven weeks, Flair and Steamboat set a standard for championship wrestling that is still used to judge long-form in-ring storytelling.
external_links: WWE.com: Flair and Steamboat on their famous trilogy (https://www.wwe.com/classics/wcw/ric-flair-ricky-steamboat-trilogy-interview); Chi-Town Rumble (Wikipedia) (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chi-Town_Rumble)
components: 1989-02-20 Steamboat wins the championship (Chi-Town Rumble, UIC Pavilion, Chicago); 1989-04-02 The two-out-of-three-falls rematch (Clash of the Champions VI: Ragin' Cajun, Louisiana Superdome, New Orleans); 1989-05-07 Flair regains the championship (WrestleWar '89, Nashville)

title: Bull Nakano vs. Aja Kong: The 1990 Cage Match
description: A no-referee steel cage match for the WWWA World Championship that showcased the intensity of women's wrestling in Japan at the start of the 1990s.
source_material: AJW Wrestlemarinepiad 1990 broadcast, Yokohama, 14 November 1990; Cagematch match database; retrospective reviews (Quebrada, The Indy Wrestling Experience)
context_statement: This cage match set a new standard for violence and drama in women's wrestling and helped define the joshi boom of the early 1990s.
external_links: Quebrada: Kanaami No Referee Death Match review (https://quebrada.net/columns/issue72/72d2.html); Retro Indy Rewatch: AJW Wrestlemarinepiad '90 (https://theindywrestlingexperience.com/2023/06/03/retro-indy-rewatch-5-ajw-wrestlemarinepiad-90-11-14-1990)

title: The Shockmaster's Debut
wrestlers_involved: Fred Ottman; Ric Flair; Sting; Davey Boy Smith; Ole Anderson
description: A planned dramatic reveal that collapsed when the debuting Shockmaster tripped through a wall on live television and lost his helmet.
source_material: WCW Clash of the Champions XXIV broadcast on TBS, 18 August 1993; WWE.com oral history "Shock and Awe"; interviews with Fred Ottman (Pro Wrestling Stories)
context_statement: The Shockmaster's trip turned a major reveal into one of wrestling's best-known blunders and remains a case study in how live production can undo a character in seconds.
external_links: WWE.com: Shock and Awe, the oral history of the Shockmaster incident (https://www.wwe.com/inside/shockmaster-incident-oral-history); Pro Wrestling Stories: Fred Ottman's side of the story (https://prowrestlingstories.com/interviews/the-shockmaster-fred-ottman/)

title: Mitsuharu Misawa vs. Toshiaki Kawada, 3 June 1994
description: A 35-minute Triple Crown defence at the Nippon Budokan that became the benchmark for the escalating, near-fall-driven style of 1990s All Japan Pro Wrestling.
source_material: AJPW Super Power Series broadcast, Nippon Budokan, Tokyo, 3 June 1994; Cagematch match database; contemporary and retrospective reviews (F4W Online, Fightful)
context_statement: Built on years of shared history between former partners, this match became the reference point for the "King's Road" style and is still cited as one of the greatest matches ever wrestled.
external_links: F4W Online: Daily Pro Wrestling History (06/03) (https://www.f4wonline.com/news/other-wrestling/daily-pro-wrestling-history-all-time-classic-misawa-vs-kawada-match); Mitsuharu Misawa (Wikipedia) (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mitsuharu_Misawa)

title: Guerrero & Barr vs. El Hijo del Santo & Octagón: Hair vs. Masks
wrestlers_involved: Eddie Guerrero; Art Barr; El Hijo del Santo; Octagón
description: A two-out-of-three-falls lucha de apuestas at When Worlds Collide that introduced many American viewers to the drama of lucha libre.
source_material: AAA/WCW When Worlds Collide pay-per-view broadcast, Los Angeles Memorial Sports Arena, 6 November 1994; Cagematch match database; Pro Wrestling Torch and F4W Online retrospectives
context_statement: Shown on American pay-per-view, this hair-versus-masks match brought lucha libre storytelling to a new audience and became the defining match of Los Gringos Locos.
external_links: AAA When Worlds Collide (Wikipedia) (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AAA_When_Worlds_Collide); Pro Wrestling Torch: Nov. 6 in history (https://www.pwtorch.com/artman2/publish/Torch_Today_2/article_74386.shtml)

title: King, from Tekken
wrestlers_involved: Seiichi Ishii (character designer); Tiger Mask (referenced); Fray Tormenta (referenced)
description: A jaguar-masked wrestler in Namco's Tekken whose look, moves and backstory pay direct homage to professional wrestling and lucha libre.
source_material: Tekken arcade game (Namco, Japanese release 9 December 1994); King (Tekken) and Tekken (video game) on Wikipedia; Tekkenpedia
context_statement: King brought a masked professional wrestler into one of the most successful fighting-game series, carrying wrestling's look and holds to a worldwide gaming audience for three decades.

title: Hulk Hogan Joins The Outsiders: The Birth of the nWo
wrestlers_involved: Hulk Hogan; Scott Hall; Kevin Nash; Randy Savage; Sting; Lex Luger
description: Hulk Hogan's turn against the fans at Bash at the Beach 1996, which created the New World Order and drove WCW to the top of the ratings.
source_material: WCW Bash at the Beach pay-per-view, Ocean Center, Daytona Beach, Florida, 7 July 1996; WWE.com history of WCW; Uproxx and Wrestling Inc retrospectives
context_statement: Hogan's heel turn turned The Outsiders' invasion into the New World Order, the storyline that powered WCW's long ratings lead over the WWF in the Monday Night Wars.
external_links: Bash at the Beach (1996) (Wikipedia) (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bash_at_the_Beach_(1996)); Uproxx: 20 years ago today, Hulk Hogan joined the nWo (https://uproxx.com/?p=1662020)

title: The Montreal Screwjob
wrestlers_involved: Bret Hart; Shawn Michaels; Vince McMahon
description: The infamous real-life double-cross of Bret Hart by Vince McMahon at Survivor Series 1997, forever altering the landscape of professional wrestling.
source_material: WWF Survivor Series 1997 pay-per-view broadcast, Molson Centre, Montreal; Wrestling Observer Newsletter (November 17, 1997); Bret Hart, Hitman (2007); Wrestling with Shadows (1998)
context_statement: Vince McMahon's secret order to end the match against his champion's will became the most notorious finish in wrestling history, and its fallout gave rise to the Mr. McMahon character at the centre of the Attitude Era.

title: The Fingerpoke of Doom
wrestlers_involved: Hulk Hogan; Kevin Nash; Tony Schiavone; Mick Foley
description: A WCW Championship match that ended with a finger poke and an nWo reunion, on the same night WCW's commentary gave away the WWF's rival title change.
source_material: WCW Monday Nitro broadcast, Georgia Dome, Atlanta, 4 January 1999; WWF Raw (taped), same night; WWE.com and Awful Announcing retrospectives; Mick Foley's later comments (Sky Sports)
context_statement: Two booking decisions on one night, a meaningless title change and a spoiled rival result, became the standard case study of how WCW lost the Monday Night Wars.
external_links: WWE.com: Mick Foley and Kevin Nash on Jan. 4, 1999 (https://www.wwe.com/classics/foley-nash-jan-4-1999); Fingerpoke of Doom (Wikipedia) (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fingerpoke_of_Doom)

title: Heroes of Wrestling
event_name: Heroes of Wrestling pay-per-view, Casino Magic, Bay St. Louis, Mississippi
wrestlers_involved: Jake Roberts; Yokozuna; King Kong Bundy; Jim Neidhart
description: A one-off pay-per-view built on stars of the 1980s that collapsed through poor planning, and is widely remembered as one of the worst wrestling events ever broadcast.
source_material: Heroes of Wrestling pay-per-view, Casino Magic, Bay St. Louis, Mississippi, 10 October 1999; Slam Wrestling contemporary review; PWInsider and Pro Wrestling Torch retrospectives; Heroes of Wrestling (Wikipedia)
context_statement: Heroes of Wrestling showed that famous names alone cannot carry a show, and that a promotion must plan for the condition and readiness of the performers it books.
external_links: Slam Wrestling: Heroes PPV a disappointment (https://slamwrestling.net/report/heroes-ppv-a-disappointment/); Heroes of Wrestling (Wikipedia) (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heroes_of_Wrestling)

title: Beyond the Mat
wrestlers_involved: Barry W. Blaustein (director); Mick Foley; Terry Funk; Jake Roberts; Vince McMahon
description: A feature documentary that followed three wrestlers at different stages of their careers and showed mainstream audiences the physical and personal cost of the business.
source_material: Beyond the Mat (documentary, dir. Barry W. Blaustein; US theatrical release 17 March 2000); Slam Wrestling and TV Guide coverage of the WWF dispute
context_statement: Beyond the Mat was one of the first feature documentaries to show wrestling's hidden costs to a general audience, and the WWF's efforts to distance itself from it became part of its story.
external_links: Beyond the Mat (Wikipedia) (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beyond_the_Mat); Slam Wrestling: Beyond the Mat embroiled in controversy (https://slamwrestling.net/news/beyond-the-mat-embroiled-in-controversy/)

title: WrestleMania X-Seven: Stone Cold vs. The Rock
wrestlers_involved: Stone Cold Steve Austin; The Rock; Vince McMahon
description: The main event of WrestleMania X-Seven marking the end of the Attitude Era.
source_material: WWF WrestleMania X-Seven pay-per-view broadcast, Reliant Astrodome, Houston, Texas
context_statement: Stone Cold Steve Austin's heel turn alongside Mr. McMahon in the main event closed the Attitude Era's defining rivalry, days after the WWF's purchase of WCW.

title: Nacho Libre
wrestlers_involved: Jared Hess (director); Jack Black; Fray Tormenta (inspiration and cameo)
description: A Hollywood comedy about a friar who secretly wrestles as a luchador, loosely based on the real-life priest and wrestler Fray Tormenta.
source_material: Nacho Libre (dir. Jared Hess, Paramount Pictures; US release 16 June 2006); Slash Film on Fray Tormenta; Slam Wrestling review
context_statement: Nacho Libre carried lucha libre's masks, rituals and underdog stories to a mainstream film audience, through a story drawn from a real wrestling priest.
external_links: Slash Film: the real story behind Nacho Libre (https://www.slashfilm.com/2063838/jack-black-comedy-nacho-libre-true-story-explained-fray-tormenta); Slam Wrestling: Nacho Libre review (https://slamwrestling.net/reviews/nacho-libre-goes-for-broke-with-broad-comedy/)

title: Being The Elite
wrestlers_involved: Matt Jackson; Nick Jackson; Kenny Omega; Cody Rhodes
description: A weekly YouTube series made by wrestlers themselves, which built an audience outside any promotion's control and helped lead to All In and the founding of AEW.
source_material: Being The Elite, YouTube series (first episode 5 May 2016); TheTVDB episode list; ProWrestling.net, Sports Illustrated and F4W Online coverage
context_statement: Being The Elite showed that wrestlers could build their own audience directly online, and the following it helped create led to All In in 2018 and the founding of All Elite Wrestling in 2019.
external_links: Sports Illustrated: the Young Bucks on bringing back Being The Elite (https://www.si.com/fannation/wrestling/aew/the-young-bucks-talk-about-bringing-back-being-the-elite); F4W Online: Young Bucks release first Being The Elite video since 2023 (https://www.f4wonline.com/news/aew/young-bucks-bte-return-october-2023)

title: Kazuchika Okada vs. Kenny Omega, Wrestle Kingdom 11
description: An IWGP Heavyweight Championship match at the Tokyo Dome that drew international attention to New Japan Pro-Wrestling in the streaming era.
source_material: NJPW Wrestle Kingdom 11, Tokyo Dome, 4 January 2017 (NJPW World stream; later shown on AXS TV); ESPN, F4W Online and Fox Sports coverage
context_statement: Okada and Omega's first meeting became the most discussed match of the streaming era and the start of a rivalry that helped make New Japan a global promotion.
external_links: ESPN: Okada and Omega put on a show at Wrestle Kingdom 11 (https://africa.espn.com/wwe/story/_/id/18413480/okada-omega-put-show-wrestle-kingdom-11-new-japan-pro-wrestling); Wrestle Kingdom 11 (Wikipedia) (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wrestle_Kingdom_11)
